description: Implement a language-agnostic mutation testing framework using TDD.

tasks.title: Validate mutation plan against schema
tasks.description: We create a Lua function that runs jsonschema.
acceptance_criteria: Use jsonschema to validate tests/data/mutation-plan.json against schemas/mutation-plan.schema.json.
An invalid mutation-plan.json (e.g., missing required field) fails validation with a non-zero exit.

tasks.title: Apply a single mutation to a source file
tasks.description: Implement a Lua function that reads a source file, applies one mutation from the mutation plan (replacing original text with replacement text at the specified location), and writes the result to a temporary file.
acceptance_criteria: Applying a CONSTANT_NUMERIC_FLIP mutation replaces the target text in the source file.
The original source file remains unchanged after mutation.

tasks.title: Respect mutation location fields (start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col)
tasks.description: When the same original text appears multiple times — the mutation should only be applied at the exact location indicated by start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation whose original text appears multiple times in the source file is only applied at the specified row/col location, not at other occurrences.
A mutation whose original text does NOT match the text at the specified row/col location reports an error (the mismatch indicates the mutation candidate is stale or the source has changed).
The replacement text is inserted at the correct column boundary within the specified row, replacing exactly the range [start_col, end_col).

tasks.title: Run a test command and report mutant outcome
tasks.description: A Lua function that executes a test command, prints whether the mutant survived or was killed, and returns a boolean.
acceptance_criteria: When the test command exits with 0 (all tests pass), the function prints 👾 survived and returns false.
When the test command exits non-zero (at least one test fails), the function prints 🏹 killed and returns true.

tasks.title: Orchestrate the mutation testing loop
tasks.description: apply_mutations_from_plan is the orchestrator. It reads a mutation plan from a JSON file, applies each mutation one at a time to the original source file (in place), runs the test command after each, prints per-mutation outcome, and writes a final JSON report with killed/survived results.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mutation plan JSON file and a test command, apply_mutations_from_plan applies each mutation individually to the source file (in place), runs the test command, and prints 🏹 killed or 👾 survived for each mutation.
Each mutation is applied to the original source — not to the result of a previous mutation. The source is reverted between mutations via git checkout.
A JSON report is written to report_path after all mutations are processed, containing the original mutation records with an additional "killed": true|false field per entry.
The report file is valid JSON matching the mutation record structure except for the added killed field.
After apply_mutations_from_plan completes, the source files are restored to their original state.
